- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward slightly to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2), model often overcorrects downward — increase forecast by 1–2% to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently overestimates short-term price drops after recent spikes — reduce forecast by 3–5% for 3–5 day horizons following sharp price increases.  
- Model underestimates mean reversion in medium-term (10–30 day) forecasts — add 1–3% upward bias to align with historical mean reversion patterns.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–4% in bullish sentiment periods — apply +1.5% to +3% upward adjustment if sentiment > 0.1 over last 5 days.  
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, adjust forecast 2–4 days ahead to reflect sentiment momentum.
